industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view: Utilities integrated moves to Overweight this week on the first European power-price reading in a month (Nordic power forwards up, Fortum's 22-year nuclear agreement with Google; Danske Bank, 28 October), Regulated networks stays Neutral and Renewable generators stays Underweight because the ten-year above 5% is the row's discount rate. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, D prior, DISAGREES with the sector move; rate-sensitives lagged on the week (Outset Global). Counter-case for B: pricing-power defensives are the rotation's destination; for D: the tape. Moves to B if a second power-price reading arrives with the industry's relative strength leaving D.

sector.key: E.3. Utilities - renewable generators and developers
sector.why: Underweight, from Neutral, correcting a relabel. The C on this row was written for the old 'Water and other non-power' Sector; the row now holds the renewable generators and developers, the debt-funded, longest-duration, most capex-dependent end of utilities, which is exactly the case the prior E.2 reason described and the regime punishes. Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): higher real yields are the direct headwind to a build-out financed at the margin, and no non-AI demand theme (electrification included) was spoken to by any source this week. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: F now, F prior, agrees. Counter-case: power is a political constraint on data centres and the energy shock lifts power prices for every generator; thirteen stocks, none in the MI Pool. Back to C if the Fed path is marked down and the sector's relative strength leaves F.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the re-test written last week (Neutral against Underweight after the Bank of England's decision and guidance on 5-Nov-26) could not run, because no source in the pack reports the outcome; the only United Kingdom items are undated headlines (the pound firmer on policy divergence; shoppers 'more upbeat than their European counterparts', City AM, against a GfK 'weakens in November' headline most likely from 2025). Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). The Budget read of last week stands: a UK-specific fiscal tail risk removed without lowering the rate; 22 of the Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Counter-case unchanged: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance when the 5-Nov-26 decision is read, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.
